'''Kamaluddin Ahmed''' (15 April 1939 – 10 June 2014), [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]], was a [[Pakistani]] [[particle physicist]] and a [[professor]] of physics at the [[Quaid-e-Azam University]].

==Early life and career==
Kamaluddin Ahmed was born in [[Delhi]], [[British India]] in 1939.<ref name=COMSATS/> He completed his Ph.D degree from [[London University]] in 1966.

Ahmed worked for the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) beginning in 1962 and remained associated with [[Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science & Technology]] (PINSTECH) until 1967.<ref name=Nation>[https://nation.com.pk/national/12-Jun-2014/veteran-particle-physicist-prof-kamaluddin-ahmed-passes-away Veteran physicist Prof. Kamaluddin Ahmed passes away] The Nation (newspaper), Published 12 June 2014; Retrieved 18 December 2020</ref> Beginning in 1966,<ref name=COMSATS>[http://comsats.org/?p=3558 CIIT holds conference in honour of late Prof. Kamaluddin Ahmed] COMSATS Institute of Information Technology website, Published 19 August 2014, Retrieved 18 December 2020</ref> he studied at the [[University of London]] under [[Abdus Salam]] and [[Paul Taunton Matthews]]. He served as an advisor in the Physics department at [[COMSATS Institute of Information Technology]] from 2002 to 2013.<ref name=COMSATS/>

He taught physics at [[Quaid-e-Azam University]] for over 30 years, starting in December 1967 and retiring in April 1999, performed research at the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in [[Dubna]],<ref name=COMSATS/> and was a Fellow of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] in 1974–75.<ref name=COMSATS/>

==Honours==
Kamaluddin Ahmed was elected as a fellow of the [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] in 2002,<ref>[https://www.paspk.org/deceased-fellows/ Kamaluddin Ahmed was elected fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences in 2002] Pakistan Academy of Sciences website, Retrieved 18 December 2020</ref><ref name=Nation/> and in 1979 and 1983 was invited to suggest nominations for the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]]. He also served as a senior research associate member with the [[Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] beginning in 1991,<ref name=Nation/> and as president of the [[Pakistan Physics Society]].

==Awards and recognition==
* [[Pride of Performance]] Award by the [[President of Pakistan]] in 2001.<ref name=COMSATS/>

==Death and legacy==
Ahmed died of [[hepatitis]] on 10 June 2014, while visiting relatives in the United States.<ref name=COMSATS/> A conference was held in his honor at the [[COMSATS Institute of Information Technology]] on 27 June 2014 to pay tribute to him. The event was attended by many physicists and members of the scientific community.<ref name=COMSATS/><!--Yes, it says "reference"; they clearly meant "conference"-->
